facts.text: Rockefeller opened the resort in the 1950s on a former plantation.
facts.excerpt: When developer Laurance S. Rockefeller opened his resort in the 1950s, he took care to preserve what made the former plantation, and Puerto Rico, special.

facts.text: In Rockefeller's original resort, buildings were no taller than palm trees.
facts.excerpt: Buildings were no taller than palm trees.

facts.text: Signature dishes at COA restaurant carry the flavor of Mi Brasa, a traditional Spanish wood-burning oven.
facts.excerpt: signature dishes carry the flavor of Mi Brasa, a traditional, Spanish wood-burning oven.

facts.text: La Cava at COA restaurant is a wine cellar with 690 labels and 3,200 bottles, which the resort describes as the largest wine cellar in Puerto Rico.
facts.excerpt: With its 690 labels and 3,200 bottles, the CAVA wine cellar offers one of the largest wine lists in the Caribbean and the largest wine cellar in Puerto Rico.

facts.text: The Treehouse Dinner is a private dining experience for two people, usually recommended for couples.
facts.excerpt: Treehouse Dining experience is a very intimate experience and usually recommended for couples, as the space is limited and only fits two people.

facts.text: A residential kitchen at La Cocina Gourmet hosts hands-on, chef-led cooking classes and five-course themed wine dinners.
facts.excerpt: hosts hands-on, chef-led cooking classes showcasing local, seasonal ingredients and five-course themed wine dinners.

facts.text: Spa Botánico treatments are performed amid gardens and shaded treetops.
facts.excerpt: A fragrant apothecary filled with herbs and flowers is the portal to this hidden sanctuary where treatments are performed amid lush gardens and shaded treetops.

facts.text: Spa Botánico is a five-acre sanctuary that pairs local Puerto Rican ingredients with indigenous soothing traditions.
facts.excerpt: The five-acre sanctuary pairs local Puerto Rican ingredients with indigenous soothing traditions

facts.text: Spa Botánico offers a Treehouse Massage amid the treetops.
facts.excerpt: Treehouse Massage

facts.text: A 100-year-old Ficus tree stands at the entrance to Spa Botánico.
facts.excerpt: A 100-year-old Ficus tree welcomes you at the Spa Botanico entrance.

facts.text: The Rockefeller Nature Trail is an 11-mile trail that runs past the two golf courses, along sandy beaches and through tree-shaded forests.
facts.excerpt: this 11-mile trail takes guests past the two courses, along the soft sandy beaches, and through tree-shaded forests

facts.text: The Rockefeller Nature Trail can be explored on foot, by bike or with a golf cart.
facts.excerpt: Named after the resort's original developer Laurance S. Rockefeller, the trail can be explored on foot, by bike or with a golf cart.

facts.text: The resort has two pools, both with direct access to the beach.
facts.excerpt: The resort’s two pools offer distinct experiences, both with direct access to Dorado’s golden sands.

facts.text: The pool at Encanto Beach Club is the family-oriented pool.
facts.excerpt: The lively energy at Encanto Beach Club is perfect for families.

facts.text: Positivo has an infinity-edge pool.
facts.excerpt: Positivo, the infinity-edge pool is serene and scenic.

facts.text: The Naturalist Experience offers scheduled outdoor group experiences for children and adults, with reservations required.
facts.excerpt: Dorado Beach's Naturalist Experience

facts.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
facts.excerpt: This hotel does not provide shuttle service.
